summary: Reproduced that exact candidate 69a812d retains a public ver selector while only one FA3 operator is wired. Removed ver from both wrappers instead of inventing an unavailable FA2 dispatch, while preserving the candidate's device-aware validation, numeric CUDA-version check, supported SM8x/SM90 contract, missing-cache guard, and pinned native correction.

tests.what_was_measured: Exact candidate failing-before: 2 failed, 14 passed; both public wrappers still exposed ver. Remaining contract checks passed.
Passing-after: 16 passed; signatures no longer expose ver, and both wrappers retain input-device validation before the instrumented native boundary.
Changed Python source and regression test compile successfully.

gpu_execution.evidence: Prepared interpreter is torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2 with torch.version.cuda=None; no NVIDIA GPU, nvcc, cuobjdump, or CUDA flash_ops build was available.

remaining_limitations: The pinned SM8x native correction was not rebuilt or numerically executed in this ROCm-only environment.
SM86-cubin execution on SM89 was not independently inspected or run; SM8x support was retained rather than changed based on unavailable local CUDA hardware.
Removing ver is an intentional public API correction: callers that previously passed it must stop doing so; no FA2 operation is wired to these wrappers in the pinned source.
